findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for and what problem it solves. That answers "what is it" and "why does it matter" before anything else on the page.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable.

findings.text: This is Athena's home URL, but the title, the "Start here" section and nearly all of the body are about a different project, firstmate. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena may not see at first that everything below the header is only a sample of Athena's output.
findings.source:
/

Start here

"The three parts below say what firstmate is..."

findings.text: The header links straight to the next steps, so a newcomer does not have to scroll past the long study to find out what to do.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself.

findings.text: The install path is concrete: prerequisites, a clone command, a setup script and a first command to try. Athena is described as written in Rust, but the prerequisites do not mention a Rust toolchain, and "run it on your repository" does not say which repository it acts on (presumably the current directory).
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "./setup.sh" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: The header shows a link meant for the site owner. To a newcomer it is noise or confusing, since they have no proposals to decide.
findings.source: Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision.

findings.text: Most terms are defined carefully, but some are not. "Wake" is defined using the word itself, and words such as endpoint, brief, crewmate and captain-held inventory appear with no definition.
findings.source: Glossary: "stale wake — A wake after which the agent inspects a worker..."; claims mention "endpoint", "brief", "crewmates", "captain-held inventory", "watcher's liveness tick"

findings.text: The bracketed claim ids link to exact file and line ranges at a pinned commit. This shows Athena's main promise, traceability, in a way a newcomer can check for themselves.
findings.source: "Each statement below ends with the id of the claim that supports it; the claims, with links to their sources, are listed at the end."

findings.text: The page says openly that nothing was run, only read. That honesty builds trust, though a newcomer may wonder how much a read-only study tells them about how well Athena does in practice.
findings.source:
Limits of this study

f1: "no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read."
